title: What does AACSB require for assurance of learning and faculty qualifications?
description: AACSB Standard 5 (assurance of learning) and Standard 3 (faculty qualifications) under the 2020 and 2026 Global Standards, with transition dates.
shortAnswer: AACSB International requires accredited business schools to run well-documented assurance of learning processes, using direct and indirect measures tied to each degree program's competency goals, and to show the results lead to curricular improvement (Standard 5). Standard 3 requires sufficient participating faculty and classifies faculty as Scholarly Academic, Practice Academic, Scholarly Practitioner, Instructional Practitioner or Additional, with minimum ratios. The 2026 Global Standards took effect on July 1, 2026, replacing the 2020 standards after a one year transition.
keyTakeaways: The AACSB Global Standards for Business Education are effective July 1, 2026. Schools visited in 2026-2027 may choose the 2020 standards or the new ones; from 2027-2028 all reviews use the Global Standards.
Standard 5.1 requires direct and indirect measures tied to competency goals "as opposed to simple satisfaction measures," with results that lead to curricular improvement.

Standard 3 sets normal minimums of 40 percent Scholarly Academic faculty and 90 percent SA, PA, SP and IP faculty, plus participating faculty delivering at least 75 percent of teaching overall and 60 percent in each discipline.
From visits in 2029-30, maintaining any qualified faculty status also requires meeting the school's teaching effectiveness criteria; faculty who do not are classified as Additional.
Initial accreditation schools must complete Table 5-1 for every degree program and meet the faculty ratios without relying on high quality outcomes as a substitute.
jurisdiction: International (AACSB accredited business schools in all countries)
regulator: AACSB International (the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business)
appliesTo: Business schools holding or seeking AACSB business accreditation, in any country
Deans, associate deans and assurance of learning coordinators
Faculty who teach in degree programs within the accreditation scope, including adjunct and visiting faculty
Providers of stackable microlearning credentials and significant non-degree executive education within the school

sections.heading: Which AACSB standards apply as at November 2026?

blocks.text: The [AACSB Global Standards for Business Education](https://www.aacsb.edu/educators/global-standards) are the current standards, effective July 1, 2026. They replace the 2020 Guiding Principles and Standards for Business Accreditation, which took effect on July 28, 2020 and were last updated on February 28, 2025.

AACSB's [standards refresh timeline](https://www.aacsb.edu/educators/accreditation/standards-refresh) records an exposure draft in January 2026, a vote by the Accreditation Council in April 2026 and adoption in July 2026, followed by a one year transition:

items: **School visit year 2026-2027:** schools may be reviewed under the 2020 standards or the Global Standards.
**School visit year 2027-2028 and later:** review is under the Global Standards.

blocks.text: Standard numbers did not change for the topics on this page: Standard 3 still covers faculty and professional staff resources, and Standard 5 still covers assurance of learning. AACSB's Global Standard-Setting Framework now puts the standards on a structured five year review cycle.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects AACSB documents as at November 2026. The Interpretive Guidance that accompanies the Global Standards is available to members only and was not reviewed here.

sections.heading: What does Standard 5 require for assurance of learning?

blocks.text: Standard 5 requires a documented system that proves learners achieve each degree program's competencies and uses the evidence to improve the curriculum. The 2026 text of Standard 5.1 reads: schools "use well-documented assurance of learning (AoL) processes that include direct and indirect measures for ensuring the quality of all degree programs that are deemed in scope for accreditation purposes."
The basis for judgment for Standard 5.1 adds the operating detail:

items: Competencies derive from the school's mission and strategy; learning objectives derive from competencies.
Competencies and curriculum management reflect currency of knowledge and the expectations of employers, alumni, learners, the university and policymakers.

Both direct and indirect measures appear across the school's portfolio. Each school sets the proportion by program, and some programs may be assessed only by direct or only by indirect measures if the school gives its rationale.
Where competencies are not achieved, the school provides evidence of remediation.
AoL involves "meaningful and broad faculty participation."
Programs launched since the last review need a documented AoL plan with a timeline for gathering and analyzing data.

blocks.text: The remaining parts extend assurance beyond core degrees. Standard 5.2 requires equivalent outcomes for the same degree regardless of location or modality, with competency-based education credit normally assured by direct assessment. Standard 5.3 covers stackable microlearning credentials. Standard 5.4 covers non-degree executive education that generates more than 5 percent of the school's total annual revenue.

sections.heading: What changed in Standard 5 between 2020 and 2026?

blocks.text: Two changes are material, according to AACSB's summary of key changes. First, Standard 5.1 now states that direct and indirect measures must be tied to specific competency goals rather than satisfaction measures alone. Second, the executive education threshold in 5.4 is now measured against more than 5 percent of annual revenue, where the 2020 text referred to "total annual resources."

For assessment designers the first change is the significant one. An end of program survey asking graduates how confident they feel no longer counts as AoL evidence unless each item maps to a stated competency. The [learning objectives vs learning outcomes](/compare/learning-objectives-vs-learning-outcomes) distinction and an [assessment blueprint](/glossary/assessment-blueprint) are the practical tools for making that mapping visible.

sections.heading: What does Standard 3 require of faculty qualifications?

blocks.text: Standard 3 requires enough engaged faculty and a qualification system that classifies every faculty member by initial preparation and sustained activity. Standard 3.2 sets four qualified categories and one residual category.

blocks.caption: AACSB faculty qualification categories under Standard 3.2 of the 2026 Global Standards
head: Category
Initial qualification
Maintenance
rows: Terminal academic degree in a field closely related to teaching
Sustained scholarly activity, including some peer reviewed journal articles
Terminal academic degree in a field closely related to teaching
Sustained professional engagement involving business and management practice
Master's degree in a closely related field plus substantial professional experience
Master's degree in a closely related field plus substantial professional experience
Does not meet the school's criteria for SA, PA, SP or IP

blocks.text: Several fixed periods apply. A newly conferred terminal degree qualifies a person as SA or PA for six years from conferral. A doctoral student who has reached all-but-dissertation status counts as SA for three years. In limited cases, SP or IP status may be granted without a master's degree if the depth and complexity of professional experience compensates, and the school must make its case.

The ratios are normal minimums: 40 percent SA and 90 percent SA, PA, SP and IP combined, across the accredited unit and in each discipline offering degrees or majors. Standard 3.1 separately expects participating faculty to deliver at least 75 percent of teaching across the school and at least 60 percent within each discipline. Schools seeking initial accreditation must meet the ratios outright.

sections.heading: When does the teaching effectiveness requirement start?

blocks.text: The teaching effectiveness requirement in Standard 3.2 applies to visits from 2029-30. The standard states that "maintenance of status requires meeting both engagement activities appropriate to the classification and the school's established teaching effectiveness criteria," and that faculty who do not meet both are classified as Additional.

AACSB's summary describes this as a three year ramp-up period. The former Standard 7.3 on faculty currency in discipline and pedagogy moved into Standard 3.2. AACSB does not prescribe teaching effectiveness metrics, states that measures must align with local policies, labor agreements and privacy rules, and does not require disclosure of confidential individual evaluations to peer review teams.

sections.heading: How can a school map Standards 3 and 5 to evidence?

blocks.text: The table below is an original mapping of AACSB obligations to the role that owns them, the cycle on which they recur and the evidence a peer review team would expect. It draws on the suggested documentation for each standard.

blocks.text: The structure is the same as any [curriculum map](/guides/how-to-build-a-curriculum-map): every competency has a place it is taught, a place it is assessed and a record of what happened next.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry defines each competency goal, its learning objectives and its assessment points before courses are written, so the curriculum map and the AoL evidence come from the same structure. When an assessment shows a gap, the affected objectives and courses can be traced directly instead of reconstructed for the next visit.

faqs.q: Can a school still be reviewed under the 2020 AACSB standards?
faqs.a: Only in the 2026-2027 visit year. AACSB's transition plan lets schools visited in 2026-2027 choose between the 2020 standards and the Global Standards for Business Education. From the 2027-2028 visit year, all reviews are conducted under the Global Standards effective July 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Does AACSB accept indirect measures alone for some programs?
faqs.a: Yes, with a rationale. The basis for judgment for Standard 5.1 allows some programs, such as small, specialized or interdisciplinary programs, to be assessed only through indirect measures, provided the school explains its choice and both measure types appear across its overall portfolio. Indirect evidence must still relate to the program's stated competencies.

No. AACSB International is a membership association that accredits business schools through peer review. Accreditation is voluntary, but it is widely used as a quality signal. Schools must also meet their national or regional regulator's rules, and AACSB allows relevant parts of those quality assurance processes to be used in AoL documentation where consistent with its expectations.

faqs.q: What happens to faculty who do not meet the teaching effectiveness criteria?
faqs.a: From visits in 2029-30, a faculty member who meets engagement expectations but not the school's teaching effectiveness criteria is classified as Additional faculty rather than SA, PA, SP or IP. That reduces the school's qualified faculty ratios, so the criteria need to be defined and applied well before the visit.
